football_evidence.question: Can Syracuse’s pass defense slow Louisville’s passing game?
football_evidence.assessment: EdgeDesk’s number is 6.8 points closer to Syracuse than the line, and EdgeDesk cannot account for most of that: its own breakdown accounts for about 2.2 of the 6.8 points. The measured football evidence leans toward Louisville, not toward EdgeDesk’s number. Treat the gap as an open research question, not as an edge.
supporting: When Syracuse has the ball (the line of scrimmage on running plays): Syracuse’s offense is stopped at or behind the line on 18.3% of its runs, and Louisville’s defense stops 9.1% of opponent runs at or behind the line (FBS average 17.4%).

When Syracuse has the ball (big plays through the air): Syracuse’s offense turns 13.4% of its pass plays into explosive gains, and Louisville’s defense gives up explosive gains on 9.8% of opponent pass plays (FBS average 10.4%).

When Louisville has the ball (pass protection against the pass rush): Louisville’s offense has allowed a sack on 6.4% of its dropbacks, and Syracuse’s defense sacks the quarterback on 6.4% of opponent dropbacks (FBS average 5.6%).
When Louisville has the ball (third down): Louisville’s offense converts 42.4% of its third downs, and Syracuse’s defense allows opponents to convert 27.7% of their third downs (FBS average 39.5%).
contradicting: When Syracuse has the ball (big plays on the ground): Syracuse’s offense turns 3.7% of its runs into explosive gains, and Louisville’s defense gives up explosive gains on 4.0% of opponent runs (FBS average 6.6%).
When Louisville has the ball (the run game against the run defense): Louisville’s offense averages 8.1 yards per carry, and Syracuse’s defense allows 5.8 yards per carry (FBS average 5.1).

When Louisville has the ball (big plays on the ground): Louisville’s offense turns 14.9% of its runs into explosive gains, and Syracuse’s defense gives up explosive gains on 7.9% of opponent runs (FBS average 6.6%).

When Louisville has the ball (big plays through the air): Louisville’s offense turns 14.8% of its pass plays into explosive gains, and Syracuse’s defense gives up explosive gains on 9.6% of opponent pass plays (FBS average 10.4%).
quarterbacks: Steve Angeli has completed 58 of 104 passes (55.8%) for 720 yards, 6.9 yards per attempt, 4 touchdowns and 4 interceptions in three games for Syracuse, and has been sacked on 8 of 112 dropbacks.
Amari Odom has completed 37 of 48 passes (77.1%) for 383 yards, 8.0 yards per attempt, 6 touchdowns and 2 interceptions in three games for Syracuse, and has been sacked on 2 of 50 dropbacks.

Lincoln Kienholz has completed 108 of 156 passes (69.2%) for 1,538 yards, 9.9 yards per attempt, 10 touchdowns and 1 interception in six games for Louisville, and has been sacked on 11 of 167 dropbacks.
